messages:
ashley: Heads up — SOC flagged a bunch of partner SIEM exports. We need a quick proposal to 1) demarcate who can request/export security logs, 2) define retention tiers for exported artifacts, and 3) clarify KMS unwrap/JIT flow for analysts. cc @ben @priya
ben: Can you list which export sinks/patterns? is this about scheduled bulk exports or ad-hoc snapshots?
ashley: Both. Examples: daily partner CSV drops (S3), ad-hoc forensic snapshots (one-offs), and API pulls we allow for vendors. SOC wants partners to only ever get tokenized/masked data unless explicit JIT approval.
priya: For triage we need raw fields like src_ip, user_id sometimes. Can we gate raw exports behind an escalation workflow instead of blanket access?
sam: +1. For incident response we need a fast path but auditable. My suggestion: create 3 export classes: `PartnerView` (redacted), `AnalystView` (masked but useful), `ForensicsView` (raw, timeboxed).
ashley: Proposed RBAC mapping (draft):
```yaml
roles:
  - name: partner_export
    grants: [export:partner_view]
    retention_days: 7
  - name: analyst_export
    grants: [export:analyst_view, ksm:request_unwrap_jit]
    retention_days: 90
  - name: forensics_export
    grants: [export:forensics_view, ksm:unwrap_with_ticket]
    retention_days: 365
```
ben: That looks reasonable. A couple of Qs: 1) how do we enforce masking for `partner_view`? 2) who can sign off on `forensics_view` unwraps?
priya: Masking: run export through the export-scrub service which applies DLP rules and field-level redaction. We should attach a digest header with `export-id` for audit if partner complains.
sam: Approval: require `oncall` + `security-approver` OR an RFC ticket from the requesting product team (JIRA SEC-4621 format). Automation idea: short-lived KMS envelope keys issued via the KMS-proxy after the approval is recorded.
sec-bot: Incident playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/forensics-export. Note: playbook requires artifact retention audit logs be stored for 5y in audit-bucket (immutable).
ashley: For KMS: we must avoid giving long-lived decryption keys to analysts. Use ephemeral unwrap via KMS-proxy + signed approval token. Example command for operator: 
```
# request unwrap (example)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"export_id":"exp-2023-09-21-001","approval_ticket":"SEC-4621"}' \
  https://kms-proxy.redwood.internal/v1/unwrap
```
ben: Should we log the plaintext access to Splunk (or S3) and tag with `requester`, `ticket`, `duration`? That will help later audits and IR postmortem.
priya: Yes. Also add a small TTL on the unwrapped artifact storage (e.g., auto-delete after 48h) unless explicitly archived with a retention justification.
sam: Edge case: what about external contractors who need short access during a vuln triage? Proposal: contractors can get `analyst_export` with additional access expiry and SCIM group membership + manager approval.
ashley: Action items: 1) ben -> inventory of active export jobs and destinations (due EOD +2). 2) priya -> draft DLP masking rules for partner_view (due +3 days). 3) sam -> KMS-proxy unwrap flow spec + audit headers (due +4 days). I'll open an RFC PR with the RBAC YAML and the approval gating flow and set a 1-week review.
ben: I'll also add a Retro simulation in next oncall rotation to validate the JIT process.
priya: If anyone needs quick examples of masking rules, ping me. I have a sample scrub config that handles PII and tokenization.
ashley: Thanks team. I'll update the RFC link once it's open: will attach playbook snippets and an export request template. :thumbsup:
